title: Real-space spectral functions of three-dimensional billion-size topological non-Hermitian matter with tensor networks
authors: Yitao Sun, Jose L. Lado, Guangze Chen
abstract: Non-Hermitian systems host a wide range of unconventional topological phenomena while large-scale simulations in finite three dimensional systems remain challenging because of the rapidly growing number of sites. In particular, higher-order topological corner modes are often studied only in small lattices, where strong finite-size effects can mask their intrinsic behavior. Here, we develop a tensor-network framework that combines quantics tensor cross interpolation with the kernel polynomial method, enabling compact representations of large non-Hermitian tight-binding Hamiltonians and direct calculations of real-space spectral functions for systems exceeding one billion lattice sites. Using this approach, we investigate three-dimensional non-Hermitian higher-order topological insulators with with structured real-space geometries. The unprecedented system size enables direct access to the macroscopic regime and allows corner-mode spectral responses to be resolved in genuinely three-dimensional systems.By tuning the loss strength, we identify distinct in-gap corner modes across weak- and strong-loss regimes.Our results establish tensor-network algorithms as a powerful strategy to perform real-space spectral calculations in exceptionally large non-Hermitian systems.
summary: The paper introduces a novel tensor-network method combining QTCI and KPM to overcome the massive computational hurdle of simulating billion-site non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. By applying this technique to 3D topological insulators, they successfully resolve corner-mode spectral features in the macroscopic limit. This establishes tensor networks as a powerful tool for analyzing complex open quantum systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is calculating real-space spectral functions for extremely large (billion-site) three-dimensional topological non-Hermitian systems.
main_result: The authors successfully developed and demonstrated a tensor-network framework capable of resolving corner-mode spectral responses in genuinely 3D, macroscopic non-Hermitian systems.
method: They combine Quantics Tensor Cross Interpolation (QTCI) with the Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM) to achieve compact representations of large Hamiltonians via Matrix Product Operator (MPO) forms.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 3D non-Hermitian higher-order topological insulators described by a tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating loss terms ($\lambda$).
key_observables: Real-space spectral functions, Local Density of States (LDOS), and the identification of distinct in-gap corner modes.
important_parameters: Loss strength ($\lambda$), system size (up to $10^9$ sites), and bond dimension ($\chi$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the large Hamiltonian can be effectively compressed into an MPO form using QTCI.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spectral functions showing isolated corner modes in weak-loss regimes and hierarchical splitting of multiple in-gap modes in strong-loss regimes, confirming localization patterns.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem (large non-Hermitian systems), develops the tensor-network methodology combining QTCI and KPM for MPO representation, applies this to 3D HOTIs with loss terms, and presents results showing spectral resolution across different loss regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses computational bottlenecks in studying complex open quantum systems by providing a scalable numerical tool (TN) for calculating spectral properties in large non-Hermitian lattices.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the tensor network algorithm and the system of interest. Panel (a) shows an example of the ten- sorization of a 3D tight-binding system. Panel (b) shows the Hermitization process of the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. With the KPM method, the spectral function of the system is obtained through MPS-MPO-MPS contraction. Panel (c) illustrates the three-dimensional BBH-type lattice models in which we demonstrate our methodology. The highlighted cor- ner region is enlarged to show the non-Hermitian potential pattern. A π flux is threaded through each plaquette via the Peierls substitution. Red and blue sites denote positive and negative imaginary on-site potentials, respectively.

FIG. 2. Spectral function with exact solvers in a small system (4096 sites). Panels (a) and (b) correspond to the weak-loss regime (λ = 2), where a single isolated corner-mode sector is observed. Panels (c)-(g) show the strong-loss regime (λ = 5), where the corner-mode manifold splits into multiple in-gap modes with distinct LDOS localization patterns. All in-gap modes are highlighted by red circles.

FIG. 3. Tensor-network results for the weak-loss regime (λ = 1.4) in the 10243 ≈109 system. Panel (a) shows the corner DOS on the complex plane with a single broadened in-gap mode separated from the bulk continuum, while (b) shows a cut of (a) with Re(E) = 0. Panel (c) shows the corner LDOS corresponding to the in-gap mode demonstrating localization within the selected corner cube of the system.

FIG. 4. Tensor-network results for the strong-loss regime (λ = 5) in the 10243 ≈109 system. Panel (a) shows the corner LDOS on the complex plane where multiple isolated modes emerge along the imaginary-energy axis. The spectral cut (b) at Re(E) = 0 further probes the hierarchical splitting of the corner modes. Panel (c)-(f) show the corner LDOS for the in-gap modes at different complex energies, revealing distinct localization patterns within the same corner cube as in Fig. 3.
